Open, complete or fail a run

Source: R/publish-products.R
soil_run_open.Rd

A run is one execution of a product version: the results published in it come from the exact source releases listed in input_release_ids (the input snapshot) and the parameters of the execution (geographic scope, options, external execution reference; never a secret).

Usage

soil_run_open(
  soil = soil_session(),
  product_version_id,
  idempotency_key,
  input_release_ids = integer(),
  parameters = list()
)

soil_run_complete(soil = soil_session(), run_id, diagnostics = list())

soil_run_fail(soil = soil_session(), run_id, diagnostics = list())

Arguments

soil

A session; the default session when omitted. Client-side: not sent to the API.

product_version_id

The id of the version (soil_product_version()). API path parameter {product_version_id} of POST /product-versions/{product_version_id}/runs.

idempotency_key

Key of the run (at most 200 characters), stable for one execution. API field idempotency_key.

input_release_ids

Ids of the source releases used by the execution (integer). API field input_release_ids.

parameters

Parameters of the execution, a named list. API field parameters.

run_id

The id of the run. API path parameter {run_id} of POST /publications/{run_id}/complete and POST /publications/{run_id}/fail.

diagnostics

Diagnostics recorded with the closing, a named list. API field diagnostics.

Value

The run: a list run_id, product_version_id, product_code, version_code, status (running, completed, failed), idempotency_key, started_at, completed_at, parameters, diagnostics, input_release_ids.

Details

soil_run_open() is idempotent: the same idempotency_key with the same parameters and input snapshot returns the run already open; with other parameters it is a soilhub_conflict_error (HTTP 409). Keep the run_id: there is no way to list runs.

soil_run_complete() closes a run whose publications are all verified (every receipt has published_count == received_count, no job left queued or running); soil_run_fail() closes it as failed, with structured diagnostics. Repeating the same closing is harmless; closing a run already closed the other way is a soilhub_conflict_error, as is completing a run with a soil-health job that did not complete.

Rights: soil:publish.

See also

Other writing: soil_product(), soil_product_version(), soil_publish_health(), soil_publish_source(), soil_publish_values(), soil_register_variable(), soil_source_validate()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
run <- soil_run_open(soil, v$product_version_id, "run-india-2026-10",
                     input_release_ids = c(12L, 14L),
                     parameters = list(country = "IND"))
# ... soil_publish_values(soil, run$run_id, ...) ...
soil_run_complete(soil, run$run_id)
} # }
